name: OK-02
label: Safe R

key_factors: R+28 partisan lean in a rural Oklahoma district
Incumbent Josh Brecheen running for reelection
Democratic challenger raised only ~$4,300 with $86 on hand
Prediction markets price Democratic win at ~2%
model.rationale: The fundamentals point overwhelmingly to Brecheen: a deep R+28 district, incumbency, and a Democratic challenger with negligible fundraising. Markets price a Republican win near certainty, and no polling or ratings suggest any reason to move off the baseline.
model.watch: Any late independent spending or polling showing unexpected Democratic strength would be the only signal worth monitoring, though none is currently evident.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Oklahoma's 2nd District is one of the most Republican-leaning seats in the country, with a partisan lean of roughly R+28. Incumbent Josh Brecheen is running for reelection after clearing his primary, and he holds a large financial advantage over Democratic nominee Brandon Wade, who has raised about $4,300 and had only $86 on hand as of the latest filing. An independent candidate, Ronnie Hopkins, is also on the ballot but has shown no measurable campaign activity.

No public polls or expert ratings cover this race, but prediction markets give Brecheen roughly a 95% chance of winning. The forecast expects a comfortable Republican victory on the order of twenty points, consistent with the district's fundamentals and the incumbent's advantages.
